tweets.text: The Supreme Court agrees, as it has defined income to mean a corporate profit. Despite the 16th Amendment, the Court ruled that direct taxes must still be apportioned. So, to harmonize an income tax that was not apportioned with the Constitution, it ruled that income must first be separated from its source before it could be taxed as an excise. Sources, like your labor, can’t be taxed. Corporations don’t pay taxes on their income; they only pay taxes on the profits derived from that income. So, in effect, the income tax is a profits tax. Therefore, like corporations, if an individual has wages, he should be able to deduct his rent, food, travel, health care, and all other personal expenses necessary to provide that labor. I would include vacations, as studies show that regular vacations help with a worker’s state of mind and ultimately make him more productive.
